mainTopic: Two ערך vows on five סלעים, the limits of ערך payments, and how many clean days a טועה needs
overview: This amud first finishes a ruling about a man who owns only five סלעים and made two ערך vows, one after the other. If he pays four toward the first vow and one toward the second, the second vow is paid but the first is not, because all five סלעים were already tied (משועבד) to the first vow. רב אדא בר אהבה then asks what happens if he made both vows in one breath: do they split the money, or does each vow claim all five? The question stays unanswered (תיקו). Next the גמרא asks why the משנה repeats that ערכין are never less than a סלע or more than fifty. It answers that the repetition teaches a payment can fall in between, following the רבנן. A new משנה then teaches that a טועה, a woman who lost track of her cycle, has her doubt resolved after no fewer than seven and no more than seventeen clean days. A ברייתא works through the cases: one, two or three days of blood need seventeen clean days. From four days on, each extra day of blood lowers the count by one, down to eleven days of blood needing nine.

steps.title: Paying four to the first vow and one to the second
steps.stepSummary: The person with five סלעים pays four toward his first ערך vow and one toward the second. Only the second vow is paid, because all five coins were tied to the first vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave four to the first vow and one to the second, he has paid the second vow but not the first, because all five coins were tied to the first vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ruling about a man with only five סלעים who made two separate ערך vows, one after the other. It looks at what happens when he splits his money four and one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first vow took hold of everything he owned, so all five סלעים were owed to it. Paying only four leaves the first vow unpaid. When he paid the second vow, one סלע was all he had, so that one coin is enough for it.

keyTerms.meaning: He has fulfilled his obligation (literally, 'he went out')
They are tied up or liened, already owed to a specific obligation
A lien, a legal claim that ties property to a debt

phrases.english: If he gave four to the first
phrases.notes: Earlier the גמרא was talking about someone who had only five סלעים and made two separate ערך vows.

phrases.english: he has not fulfilled the first
because all of them are tied to the first.
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all five coins he had when he made the first vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ruling from earlier on the daf about two separate ערך vows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With vows made one after the other, the first vow takes hold of all five סלעים. Paying four to it does not fulfill it, while one סלע fulfills the second vow.

steps.title: Two vows made at the same moment
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה asks what happens if someone with five סלעים vows his ערך twice in one statement. Do the vows split the money, or does each vow claim all five?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה asked: if he had five סלעים and said in one breath, 'Twice my ערך is upon me,' what is the law? Since he vowed both at once, maybe they take hold of the money together, so he gives two and a half to each. Or perhaps all five are fit for this vow and all five are fit for that vow?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה raises a new question. What if the two vows were made together instead of one after the other?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 1, the first vow came first and grabbed all the money. Here neither vow comes first. One side says they share, so each gets two and a half. The other side says each vow on its own reaches all five coins, so he would owe five for each.

keyTerms.meaning: He asks, raises a question he is unsure of
At one time, at the same moment
They take hold of it, they take effect on it
Or perhaps, which opens the other side of the question
Fit for, available for

phrases.english: If he had five sela in his possession
and he said, "Twice my valuation is upon me"
at one time, what is the law?
Since he vowed at one time
so he gives two and a half to this one
and two and a half to that one
or perhaps all of them are fit for this one
and all of them are fit for that one?
phrases.notes: If so, he would have to pay five סלעים for each vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the case of step 1 and changes one detail: the two vows are made together instead of one after the other.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When two ערך vows take effect together on only five סלעים, do they divide the money, or does each one claim all of it?

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves רב אדא בר אהבה's question without an answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the question with תיקו, meaning no answer is found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side of the question is proven. Both ways of seeing two vows made together stay possible.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand, meaning the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Two vows made one after the other: the first takes all five סלעים. Two vows made together: unresolved (תיקו).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question raised in step 2 without answering it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no ruling on whether two ערך vows made together split the five סלעים or each claim all five.

steps.title: Why does the משנה repeat this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of the משנה, 'there is no ערך less than a סלע or more than fifty,' and asks why it is said again.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'There is no ערך less than a סלע and not more than fifty, etc.' Why do I need this again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes a line from the end of the משנה and asks why the line is needed, since the משנה already said this at its start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא expects every line of a משנה to teach something. Repeating a rule with nothing new would be wasted words. So the repetition must hide a new lesson, which the next step will show.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed payments to the Temple when someone vows the 'value' of a person
A silver coin, the basic unit used for ערכין
Why do I need this again? A question asking why something is repeated

phrases.english: There is no valuation less than a sela

phrases.notes: 'More' means more than fifty סלעים. The 'etc.' points back to the rest of the line in the משנה.

phrases.english: Why do I need this again?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to a line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The repeated line at the end of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already said this rule at its start, so saying it again seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The repetition teaches that payments can fall in between
steps.stepSummary: The repeated line teaches that a payment can be more than one סלע and less than fifty. This matches the view of the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us: there is no payment less than a סלע, but there can be one of more than a סלע. There is no payment of more than fifty, but there can be one of less than fifty. And this unnamed משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in step 4. The repeated line teaches that a payment can land anywhere between one סלע and fifty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'no less than a סלע' suggest that more than a סלע is possible. The words 'no more than fifty' suggest that less than fifty is possible. So a person who cannot pay the full ערך pays what he can afford, even if it is more than one סלע. That is the view of the רבנן, against רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us, the formula that answers 'why is this needed?'
There is not / there is
An unnamed משנה, one that gives no author's name
In line with the view of the רבנן, the majority of the sages

steps.whatToRemember: The repeated line teaches that a ערך payment can be anywhere between one and fifty סלעים. The unnamed משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a poor person pays as much as he can afford toward his ערך, not just one סלע. It also tells us which opinion this unnamed משנה follows.

phrases.english: it is less than a sela that does not exist
but more than a sela does exist;
phrases.notes: He means a person who cannot pay the full ערך may end up paying something like two or three סלעים.

phrases.english: it is more than fifty that does not exist
but less than fifty does exist
and the unattributed ruling follows the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the repeated line in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the repeated line is not wasted, because it teaches a new rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line seemed to just repeat the limits already given at the start of the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line teaches that payments between one and fifty סלעים are possible, matching the רבנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A ערך payment is never under one סלע or over fifty, but can be any amount in between. The unnamed משנה follows the רבנן.

steps.title: New משנה: A confused woman's doubt resolves in seven to seventeen days
steps.stepSummary: The מִשְׁנָה states that the פתח for a טועה is never fewer than seven days and never more than seventeen.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who lost track of her cycle gets her 'opening' after no fewer than seven clean days and no more than seventeen.
steps.whatsHappening: A new מִשְׁנָה opens with a new topic. It sets a range: a טועה's doubt is resolved after between seven and seventeen clean days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The background is a cycle of seven ימי נדה followed by eleven ימי זיבה. A טועה saw blood but does not know where in that cycle she is. The מִשְׁנָה gives the lowest and highest number of clean days it can take until she is surely back at the start of her ימי נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who lost track of her cycle and does not know if she is in her נדה days or her זיבה days
Literally 'opening'; the point where her doubt is resolved and she is surely back at the start of her נדה days
The seven days of the cycle when blood makes her a נדה
The eleven days after the נדה days when blood can make her a זבה

steps.confusionAlert: This uses the same wording as the earlier line about ערכין, 'no less than... and no more than...'. But it is a completely different topic. It is a separate מִשְׁנָה with its own range.

phrases.english: The 'opening' for a woman unsure of her cycle is not less than seven,
phrases.notes: 'Opening' means the point where her doubt is cleared up. The numbers here count clean days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new מִשְׁנָה, unrelated to the ערכין discussion in steps 1-5 except for the similar 'no less than / no more than' form.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טועה's doubt is resolved after a minimum of seven and a maximum of seventeen clean days.

steps.title: One day of blood: her opening is seventeen days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a טועה who saw blood for one day needs seventeen clean days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a confused woman who said 'I saw blood for one day' gets her opening after seventeen days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that starts explaining the מִשְׁנָה case by case. The first case is a woman who saw blood for just one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe her one day of blood was the very first of her ימי נדה. If so, six more נדה days plus eleven זיבה days must pass, which is seventeen. Only then is she surely back at a new start. Since we must cover the longest possibility, she needs seventeen clean days.

keyTerms.meaning: Her opening, meaning the point where her doubt is resolved
'I saw impure', meaning I saw blood

phrases.english: A woman unsure of her cycle who said:

phrases.notes: She means she saw blood for one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: טוֹעָה שֶׁאָמְרָה ״יוֹם אֶחָד טָמֵא רָאִיתִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins filling in the מִשְׁנָה's range with specific cases, starting at the high end, seventeen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One day of blood requires seventeen clean days.

steps.title: Two or three days of blood: still seventeen days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: two or three days of blood also require seventeen clean days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she said 'I saw blood for two days', her opening is seventeen. If she said 'I saw blood for three days', her opening is seventeen.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with more cases. Even when she saw blood for two or three days, the answer stays at seventeen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think more days of blood would shorten the wait. But the earlier days might have been the last days of זיבה, with only the final day being the first נדה day. In that case, six נדה days and eleven זיבה days still remain, so it is still seventeen.

keyTerms.meaning: Two days
Three days

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that more days of blood always means a shorter wait. Here the worst case stays the same, so the number does not drop yet.
steps.whatToRemember: For one, two, or three days of blood, a טועה needs seventeen clean days. We always cover the worst case, where her last day of blood was the first of her ימי נדה.

phrases.notes: Maybe the first day was the last זיבה day and the second was the first נדה day. Then 6 plus 11 days are still left.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״שְׁנֵי יָמִים טָמֵא רָאִיתִי״ — פִּתְחָהּ שִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the next cases in the series, keeping the same answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two or three days of blood also require seventeen clean days, because the last day may have been the first נדה day.

steps.title: Four days of blood need sixteen clean days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that if the טועה saw blood for four days, her פתח is sixteen clean days. This is the first time the number drops below seventeen.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she says, "I saw blood for four days," she needs sixteen clean days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list. Four days of blood means she now needs sixteen clean days, not seventeen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We take the longest possible case. The first two days of blood were the end of her days of זיבה, and the other two were the first two of her seven days of נידה. She still needs five more days of נידה plus eleven days of זיבה, which makes sixteen.

keyTerms.meaning: "I saw impure": I had a flow of blood
The seven days of a woman's regular period
The eleven days between periods. Blood seen then is זיבה blood
The eleven days of זיבה that come after the seven days of נידה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think more days of blood make things stricter. Here more blood means fewer clean days, because more of her נידה days are already used up.

phrases.notes: "Her opening" means the number of clean days after which her doubt ends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's count from two or three days (seventeen) to four days, where the number first goes down.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four days of blood: sixteen clean days end her state of doubt.

steps.title: Five to eight days of blood: each extra day takes one clean day off
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on: five days need fifteen clean days, six need fourteen, seven need thirteen, and eight need twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five days of blood need fifteen clean days. Six days need fourteen. Seven days need thirteen. Eight days need twelve.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes this part of its list. For each extra day of blood, one fewer clean day is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same worst-case picture stays in place. The first two days were the end of זיבה, and every day after that is one more day of נידה already used up. Fewer נידה days are left, so the total she still needs (the rest of נידה plus eleven days of זיבה) drops by one each time. With eight days, six נידה days have passed, so she needs one more day of נידה plus eleven, which makes twelve.

keyTerms.meaning: Twelve: the clean days needed after eight days of blood

steps.whatToRemember: The rule: after the first two or three days of blood, each extra day of blood takes one day off the clean days she needs. This is because the first two days are treated as the end of זיבה and the rest as days of נידה already used up.

phrases.notes: Seven days: two at the end of זיבה, five of נידה. So two more נידה days plus eleven, which makes thirteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the same pattern as step 9, lowering the clean days by one for each extra day of blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five, six, seven and eight days of blood need fifteen, fourteen, thirteen and twelve clean days.

steps.title: Nine days of blood need eleven clean days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a טועה who saw blood for nine days needs eleven clean days as her פתח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she says, 'I saw nine impure days,' her opening is eleven clean days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going down its list. Now it covers a woman who saw blood for nine days, and it says she needs eleven clean days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes the worst case. The first two days of blood may have fallen at the end of her ימי זיבה, and the next seven may have been her ימי נידה. If so, a full eleven days of זיבה come next, so she needs eleven clean days before a new cycle could begin.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure. Here it describes days on which she saw blood.
The eleven days between one נידה cycle and the next, when bleeding can make her a זבה.
The seven days of the regular menstrual period.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's countdown from Step 10, where eight days of blood needed twelve clean days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nine days of blood need a פתח of eleven clean days.

steps.title: Ten days need ten clean days, eleven days need nine
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that ten days of blood need ten clean days, and eleven days of blood need nine clean days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she says, 'I saw ten impure days,' her opening is ten clean days. If she says eleven, her opening is nine.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives two more cases in the same list: ten days of blood and eleven days of blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worst case is the same as before. The first two days of blood may have been at the end of her ימי זיבה, and the rest covered her seven ימי נידה plus some days of the new זיבה period. Each extra day of blood uses up one more day of that זיבה period, so she needs one fewer clean day each time.

keyTerms.meaning: Her 'opening.' This is the number of clean days she must count before she can start a new, known cycle.
A woman who lost track of her cycle and does not know which days are ימי נידה and which are ימי זיבה.

steps.whatToRemember: From four days of blood onward, every extra day of blood lowers the פתח by one day: 4→16, 5→15, and so on, down to 9→11, 10→10, and 11→9.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same countdown right after the nine-day case in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten days of blood need a פתח of ten clean days, and eleven days of blood need a פתח of nine.
